Complete a target using an independently measured reference subset

Source: R/reference.R
catmech_reference.Rd

Treats the reference column as the only observed truth for the target. Every non-reference target is unavailable, regardless of its recorded value or flags. This changes the trust assumption; it does not infer a gold standard from a noisy measurement or correct missed errors without external information.

Usage

catmech_reference(
  data,
  value,
  reference,
  predictors,
  method = c("normal", "pmm", "pmm_abb"),
  donors = 5L,
  m = 20L,
  seed = 1L,
  use_recorded = FALSE,
  cluster = NULL,
  cluster_model = c("moment", "joint", "joint_marginal"),
  joint_control = list()
)

Arguments

data

A data frame; raw target measurements remain in `original`.

value

Name of the numeric target to replace in completed datasets.

reference

Name of a numeric gold-standard column, observed only where independently measured. Known reference values are preserved exactly in the completed target, including when they disagree with recorded measurements.

predictors

Explicit complete predictor names, excluding `value` and `reference`. Include the scientific outcome and relevant design variables. A raw measurement may be used only through a separate explicitly selected, complete auxiliary column. No missing proxy is filled automatically.

method

`"normal"` (default) for conditional Gaussian posterior draws, `"pmm"` for standard predictive mean matching using reference donors, or `"pmm_abb"` for the same matching on a fresh bootstrap of the donors at each imputation. See details.

donors

Nearest-donor count for matching, default five; ignored by the normal method. Fewer reference observations than donors is an error when needed.

m

Number of completions, at least two.

seed

Nonnegative integer seed, with caller RNG restored.

use_recorded

For `method = "normal"`, also use the recorded value as a linear predictor. Records with a recorded value are imputed from a model fitted on references that also have one, and records without one from a model on the predictors fitted on all references. It needs rows with both values. If every such row agrees exactly, those records keep their recorded value with no imputation uncertainty, as `spec$recorded_fit` notes and a warning says. Intervals then treat those records as correct, which can be badly wrong when a small audit simply missed the errors.

cluster

With `use_recorded = TRUE`, the name of a complete column identifying audit clusters, such as a site or facility. The imputation model then adds a random intercept for the cluster, instead of treating rows as independent. If the audit is stratified, put the strata in `predictors`, which needs some stratum with at least two audited clusters. Do not use it when the audited value will be a predictor in the analysis. See details.

cluster_model

`"moment"` preserves the existing recorded-value regression. `"joint"` explicitly selects a bivariate Gaussian model of the true target and recorded value with one shared two-dimensional site effect. It requires `method = "normal"`, `use_recorded = TRUE` and `cluster`. `"joint_marginal"` jointly models the true measurement, recorded value and complete continuous numeric predictors, allowing correlated site effects across all of them. Use [catmech_marginal_summary()] for population marginal coefficients from this model; [catmech_joint_summary()] applies to `"joint"`.

joint_control

Named list for the joint sampler: `chains = 4`, `burnin = 1000`, `iterations = 4000`, `max_iterations = 32000`, and `prior_scale = 1`. Chains must be at least four. Failed diagnostic screens restart the same seeded chains with doubled retained iterations up to the declared maximum, then fail with traces in a `catmech_convergence_error`. For `"joint"`, each chain uses a fresh R worker to isolate the backend RNG. For `"joint_marginal"`, a compiled blocked Gibbs sampler uses independent R RNG streams. Its default maximum is 64000 retained iterations per chain. It also accepts `regression_scale = 10`, the conditional matrix-normal prior scale for within- and between-site measurement regressions on the predictors. Its predictor and conditional-measurement covariance blocks have Huang–Wand priors with half-t(2) marginal standard deviations of scale `sqrt(prior_scale)` in standardized units. These are distinct from the reconstructed full covariance matrices and from the fixed inverse-Wishart prior in `"joint"`.

Value

A `catmech_result`. Its completed target contains exact gold references or imputations; the original reference column is unchanged. The `mids` observed target is the reference values with other rows missing. The manifest records `imputed_rows` explicitly, including an empty vector for full reference.

Details

Reference selection must be ignorable given the selected observed predictors, with adequate support in the reference subset. Reference values must measure the same quantity, time point and units, and are assumed exact. Unknown reference error, unmeasured selection and transport failure are not repaired. This is standard missing-data imputation using externally supplied validation information, not automatic detection of errors in unvalidated records.

With partial reference data, normal imputation delegates to `catmech_model` with categories ignored and without a quality-flag policy. PMM delegates to the same audited standard matching engine as `catmech_pmm`. Both require a full-rank reference design with positive residual degrees of freedom and variance. Complete reference data need no stochastic fit or donor support.

Partial-reference PMM is experimental sensitivity output. A held-out package benchmark found substantial interval undercoverage even with a randomly selected, accurate reference subset. As a conservative package policy, `catmech_pool_lm` requires `allow_sensitivity = TRUE` whenever reference PMM imputes any target cells, and labels its calculations `sensitivity_only`. This policy is not a general theorem about PMM, and the opt-in does not establish inferential validity. `catmech_sensitivity` already supplies an explicit sensitivity context. Complete reference data remain eligible for ordinary complete-data pooling because no target cells are imputed.

The likely cause of that undercoverage is that standard matching conditions on one fixed set of donor values, which attenuates between-imputation variance (Gaffert, Meinfelder and Bosch). `"pmm_abb"` resamples donors with replacement for each imputation, an approximate Bayesian bootstrap (Rubin and Schenker, 1986; Siddique and Belin, 2008), before the same delegated type-1 matching. It targets that variance and is not gated. It still cannot leave donor support, and it does not make matching more precise than the normal method when the normal model holds.

With `use_recorded = TRUE`, reference selection may depend on the recorded value, and linearity in the recorded value becomes an assumption. It was best or tied among reference-using methods at 25 gross errors, which distort a linear fit; [catmech_contamination()] is the alternative there.

With the default `cluster_model = "moment"`, the imputation model is the recorded-value regression plus a random intercept for the cluster. Its variance components come from moments (Henderson, 1953, method 3) on the audited rows and are drawn in each imputation, and coefficients are drawn from the generalized least squares fit given them. An unaudited cluster gets a new intercept, an audited cluster with unaudited rows gets one conditional on its residuals, and every imputed row gets normal noise. If the audited rows cannot separate the two variances, as with one row per cluster, the intercept variance is zero, with a warning. If the predictors absorb every audited cluster, as with one audited cluster per stratum, there is no estimate of between-cluster variance for unaudited clusters, and the fit is refused. Fewer than five audited clusters are refused. Pool with [catmech_pool_lm()], which uses a cluster-robust variance for such a fit. This is the usual random-intercept imputation model (Schafer and Yucel, 2002; Grund and colleagues, 2018), with a moment-based draw of the variance components in place of a full posterior. That draw is an approximation; balanced clusters alone do not make it an exact posterior draw with general predictors. Its justification is weaker with one or two large sites. It is not a new method. It assumes one normal intercept per cluster, so cluster-specific slopes and non-constant variance are not modeled. The same model is available in other software, including `mice`.

With `cluster_model = "moment"`, unaudited rows within a cluster cannot require stochastic imputation through both the recorded-present and recorded-missing paths: the current separate fits do not provide a shared cluster draw across those paths, so that request is refused. Different clusters may use different paths. Audited rows and recorded values kept deterministically after complete calibration agreement do not trigger this refusal. Resolve one pattern with reference measurements or explicitly select `cluster_model = "joint"`.

The explicit joint option uses `pan::pan` to fit `(T, W) = X B + u_site + e`, with unrestricted bivariate normal site and row covariance matrices. Observed gold values and recorded values enter as fixed observed components; unobserved components are missing data. Both responses are centered and scaled using their observed means and standard deviations, and non-intercept design columns are centered and scaled. The resolved transforms are recorded. The coefficient prior is flat. Each covariance prior is inverse Wishart with four degrees of freedom and scale `0.5 * prior_scale * I`, whose mean is `0.5 * prior_scale * I` in standardized units. These empirically scaled covariance priors are proper and substantive; they are not noninformative. Vary the declared prior scale.

Joint completions draw a single site vector conditional on the original observed components at each selected parameter draw, then draw missing targets conditional on the recorded value where available. This supports mixed recording patterns within a site and sites with no observations. Fully missing rows do not enter the fitting likelihood. The joint model has no deterministic agreement shortcut. Full-rank designs separately on gold, recorded and paired rows, two paired residual degrees of freedom, five observed sites per response, and within- and between-site residual information are supported-data requirements. They do not establish model adequacy. Joint parameter and conditional-mean traces use the existing R-hat and bulk/tail ESS screen. See `docs/JOINT_CLUSTER_METHOD.md` for assumptions and limits.

The moment-based `cluster` option is experimental. Version 0.6.0 replaced an earlier version that resampled audited clusters, in which resampling within strata understated variance. The replacement's planned test came out PARTIAL under a rule fixed in advance: on a real facility recount at a 25 audit, coverage was within its limits on eight of nine items, with 89.0 error on the three rare items ran 4 accuracy conditions failed. Treat `cluster` as a check, not a default. Read the `df` column, since very wide intervals remain possible with few audited clusters. See `validation/CLUSTERED_FIX_SYNTHESIS.md`.

In later simulations where the audited value was a predictor in the analysis and errors shifted whole clusters, the moment-based `cluster` option biased that slope toward zero and covered far less than a fit without it. The cause has not been established. [catmech_pool_lm()] warns about this use. See `validation/VARIANCE_MI_SYNTHESIS.md`. With `cluster_model = "joint_marginal"`, the continuous predictors are observed components of the same multivariate Gaussian model as the true and recorded measurements. This allows their site effects to be correlated and distinguishes marginal from within-site coefficients. Independent sites, noninformative site sizes, Gaussian joint associations, exact references and ignorable observation patterns remain assumptions. Missing, categorical, constant or aliased predictors are refused. The marginal model additionally requires at least two residual degrees of freedom and two numerically independent paired-measurement residual directions after adjusting for predictors and site indicators. This conservative support restriction protects the weak covariance prior near singular residual directions; it can exclude otherwise identifiable sparse paired designs. Population coefficient summaries include uncertainty in predictor means and covariances. An all-reference input still takes the exact-copy shortcut and does not fit a posterior for either joint summary function.

Examples

set.seed(123)
n <- 40
df <- data.frame(
  lab_val = stats::rnorm(n, 10, 2),
  age = stats::rnorm(n, 50, 10)
)
df$lab_ref <- df$lab_val + stats::rnorm(n, 0, 0.2)
df$lab_ref[11:n] <- NA
res <- catmech_reference(df, value = "lab_val", reference = "lab_ref",
                         predictors = "age", use_recorded = TRUE, m = 2, seed = 1)
summary(res)
#> <summary.catmech_result: reference_normal_recorded>
#>   Target value:    lab_val
#>   Reference:       lab_ref
#>   Predictors:      age
#>   Observations:    40
#>   Completions (m): 2
#>   Imputed rows:    30
#>   Convergence:     passed
#> 
#> Parameter diagnostics (first 8 monitors):
#> [1] parameter rhat      ess_bulk  ess_tail 
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
